title: From Paths to Trajectories: Time Scaling and Velocity Profiles

contract.reader: A student or engineer with a collision-free path from a planner who must send a timed motion to motors with speed, acceleration and jerk limits; comfortable with calculus and Python
contract.problem: A path says where but not when; the reader needs a schedule as fast as the limits allow, smooth enough for the structure, through waypoints without stopping, and verified before it reaches hardware
contract.outcome: Derive cubic and quintic scalings and shortest durations; compute trapezoidal, triangular and S-curve durations; explain the phase plane, velocity limit curve and time-optimal structure; fit natural and clamped cubic splines; check a trajectory by sampling with a provable clearance bound and fix a too-fast timing by stretching
contract.contribution: One running two-link-arm example from polynomial scaling to S-curves, a discretized time-optimal pass with measured limit violations, splines through waypoints and a sampling check that separates proof from sampling
contract.evidence: Derivations; Python listings with real output; six exercises; Bobrow et al. (1985), de Boor (2001), Flash and Hogan (1985), Kunz and Stilman (2012), Lynch and Park (2017), Pham (2014), Shin and McKay (1985)
contract.limitations: Kinematic limits only, no torque dynamics; kinodynamic planning and moving obstacles not treated; forward-backward pass approximates switching-point algorithms; illustrative limit values

findings.location: Section 5.2 recurrence and clamped end conditions, Section 6.3 stretch factor (desktop-light-18, 24); at 360 px also 2.3 and 4.1 inequalities (mobile-light-11, 21, 33)
findings.problem: At 1280 px the tridiagonal recurrence and the M_n end condition are cut and the stretch-factor result 1.1199 is hidden; at 360 px the recurrence shows only its left side
findings.whyItMatters: The recurrence and end conditions are the system the Section 5 code and Exercise 5 solve; the reader cannot check code against an invisible right-hand side; k is the result of 6.3
findings.action: Break the recurrence over two lines, put the two clamped end conditions on separate lines, put the numerical evaluation of k on its own line
findings.acceptance: On new captures the 5.2 and 6.3 displays are fully visible at 1280 px, and every listed display is fully visible at 360 px, light and dark

findings.problem: A page about velocity profiles and the phase plane has no figure; trapezoid, S-curve and the time-optimal curve must be reconstructed from prose and program output
findings.whyItMatters: Standards 6.8 prefer a line chart for change over time; the phase-plane argument of Section 4, the page's distinctive content, costs far more effort without a plot
findings.action: Add plots generated from the page's own programs: velocity and acceleration against time for the cubic, quintic, trapezoidal and S-curve profiles of the running example; the phase plane of Section 4.2 with velocity limit curve, both passes, the final scaling and the active-constraint intervals; captions say what to notice
findings.acceptance: The live page shows at least the profile plot and the phase-plane plot with captions, legible at 1280 and 360 px and correct in dark mode

findings.problem: Printed lines are wider than the code box at 1280 px; the simulated-distance check, the at-interval-end accelerations and the motion bound per sample are hidden
findings.whyItMatters: The prose repeats the numbers, but the reader is told to read them from the output
findings.action: Shorten labels or split the printed lines; re-run the programs and paste the new output
findings.acceptance: The three output blocks fit at 1280 px, or the finding is accepted as a limitation of wide output

findings.location: Opening, Conventions paragraph; listings of Sections 4.2 and 6.2
findings.problem: The page says rerunning the programs reproduces every quoted number, but the listings omit x_limit, the inverse kinematics, path, spline_eval, clearance and the printing code, so a reader cannot rerun Sections 4.2 and 6.2
findings.whyItMatters: Reads as an invitation to reproduce that the reader cannot accept for the two most interesting results
findings.action: Publish the complete programs (download or collapsed full listing) or reword to say the output comes from complete programs of which the listings show the core
findings.acceptance: The live page links the complete programs or no longer implies the reader can rerun them
